members.title: handle
members.signature: public Tokens handle(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response) throws IdentityVerificationException
members.description:
Process a request to obtain a set of `Tokens` that represent successful authentication or authorization.

This method should be called when processing the callback request to your application. It will validate authentication-related request parameters, handle performing a Code Exchange request if using the "code" response type, and verify the integrity of the ID token (if present).

**Important:** When using this API, you **must** also use `AuthenticationController.buildAuthorizeUrl(HttpServletRequest,` when building the `AuthorizeUrl` that the user will be redirected to to login. Failure to do so may result in a broken login experience for the user.

returns.description: the Tokens obtained after the user authentication.

throws.name: InvalidRequestException
throws.description: if the error is result of making an invalid authentication request.

throws.name: IdentityVerificationException
throws.description: if an error occurred while verifying the request tokens.

examples.title: Process the callback request and retrieve tokens

members.title: handle
members.signature: public Tokens handle(HttpServletRequest request) throws IdentityVerificationException
members.description:
Process a request to obtain a set of `Tokens` that represent successful authentication or authorization.

This method should be called when processing the callback request to your application. It will validate authentication-related request parameters, handle performing a Code Exchange request if using the "code" response type, and verify the integrity of the ID token (if present).

**Important:** When using this API, you **must** also use the `AuthenticationController.buildAuthorizeUrl(HttpServletRequest,` when building the `AuthorizeUrl` that the user will be redirected to to login. Failure to do so may result in a broken login experience for the user.

**Deprecated.** This method uses the `HttpSession` for auth-based data, and is incompatible with clients that are using the "id_token" or "token" responseType with browsers that enforce SameSite cookie restrictions. This method will be removed in version 2.0.0. Use `AuthenticationController.handle(HttpServletRequest,` instead.

returns.description: the Tokens obtained after the user authentication.

throws.name: InvalidRequestException
throws.description: if the error is result of making an invalid authentication request.

throws.name: IdentityVerificationException
throws.description: if an error occurred while verifying the request tokens.

members.title: buildAuthorizeUrl
members.signature: public AuthorizeUrl buildAuthorizeUrl(HttpServletRequest request, String redirectUri)
members.description:
Pre builds an Auth0 Authorize Url with the given redirect URI using a random state and a random nonce if applicable.

**Important:** When using this API, you **must** also obtain the tokens using the `AuthenticationController.handle(HttpServletRequest)` method. Failure to do so may result in a broken login experience for users.

**Deprecated.** This method stores data in the `HttpSession`, and is incompatible with clients that are using the "id_token" or "token" responseType with browsers that enforce SameSite cookie restrictions. This method will be removed in version 2.0.0. Use `AuthenticationController.buildAuthorizeUrl(HttpServletRequest,` instead.

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: the caller request. Used to keep the session context.

parameters.name: redirectUri
parameters.description: the url to call back with the authentication result.

returns.description: the authorize url builder to continue any further parameter customization.

members.title: buildAuthorizeUrl
members.signature: public AuthorizeUrl buildAuthorizeUrl(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response, String redirectUri)
members.description:
Pre builds an Auth0 Authorize Url with the given redirect URI using a random state and a random nonce if applicable.

**Important:** When using this API, you **must** also obtain the tokens using the `AuthenticationController.handle(HttpServletRequest,` method. Failure to do so will result in a broken login experience for users.

parameters.name: response
parameters.description: the HTTP response. Used to store auth-based cookies.

parameters.name: redirectUri
parameters.description: the url to call back with the authentication result.

returns.description: the authorize url builder to continue any further parameter customization.

members.description: Specify that transient authentication-based cookies such as state and nonce are created with the specified `Path` cookie attribute.

members.title: withResponseType
members.description: Change the response type to request in the Authorization step. Default value is 'code'.

parameters.name: responseType
parameters.description: the response type to request. Any combination of 'code', 'token' and 'id_token' but 'token id_token' is allowed, using a space as separator.

members.title: withJwkProvider
members.description: Sets the Jwk Provider that will return the Public Key required to verify the token in case of Implicit Grant flows. This is required if the Auth0 Application is signing the tokens with the RS256 algorithm.

members.title: withClockSkew
members.description: Sets the clock-skew or leeway value to use in the ID Token verification. The value must be in seconds. Defaults to 60 seconds.

parameters.name: clockSkew
parameters.description: the clock-skew to use for ID Token verification, in seconds.

members.title: withAuthenticationMaxAge
members.description: Sets the allowable elapsed time in seconds since the last time user was authenticated. By default there is no limit.

parameters.name: maxAge
parameters.description: the max age of the authentication, in seconds.

members.title: withLegacySameSiteCookie
members.description: Sets whether fallback cookies will be set for clients that do not support SameSite=None cookie attribute. The SameSite Cookie attribute will only be set to "None" if the reponseType includes "id_token". By default this is true.

parameters.name: useLegacySameSiteCookie
parameters.description: whether fallback auth-based cookies should be set.

members.title: withSecureCookie
members.description:
Sets whether cookies used during the authentication flow have the `Secure` attribute set or not. By default, cookies will be set with the Secure attribute if the responseType includes `id_token` and thus requires the `SameSite=None` cookie attribute set. Setting this to false will **not** override this behavior, as clients will reject cookies with `SameSite=None` unless the `Secure` attribute is set.

While not guaranteed by all clients, generally a cookie with the `Secure` attribute will be rejected unless served over HTTPS.

parameters.name: secureCookie
parameters.description: whether to always set the Secure attribute on all cookies.

members.title: fromPushedAuthorizationRequest
members.description: Executes a Pushed Authorization Request (PAR) and uses the `request_uri` to construct the authorize URL.

returns.description: the authorize URL as a string.

throws.name: InvalidRequestException
throws.description: if there is an error when making the request.

examples.title: Customize and build the authorization URL
examples.code:
String url = controller
    .buildAuthorizeUrl(request, response, "https://your-app.com/callback")
    .withConnection("google-oauth2")
    .withScope("openid profile email")
    .withAudience("https://api.your-app.com")
    .build();
response.sendRedirect(url);
